$comment: When to use each Tag variant. The component is src/styles/components/tag.css, built from Figma "Foundation – UI 2" (Tags, node 45:14; component set 45:81). Shown on the Tags page and published to public/llms.txt by `npm run tokens`.
intro: Tags label an item with a short status, category or count. They are 16px tall, come in five colors, and can be strong (filled) or outlined, with an optional 12px icon in front.

variants.label: Inverted
variants.usage: A neutral label that has to stand out, e.g. New or Beta.

variants.label: Danger
variants.usage: Errors and blocked states, e.g. Failed, Overdue, Blocked.

variants.label: Success
variants.usage: Positive or finished states, e.g. Done, Active, Paid.

variants.label: Warning
variants.usage: Needs attention but isn't broken, e.g. Pending, Expiring, Draft.

rules: Use Label; add tag--outline for the outlined style (Figma Strong=False).
Use a strong tag for the one status that matters most in a row or card, and outlined tags when several sit together, so they don't compete.
Keep labels to one or two words. Tags don't wrap or truncate.
Don't rely on color alone: the label itself must say the status.
Tags aren't interactive. For an action, use a Button.
An optional icon goes before the label: <svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#icon-<name>"></use></svg>. The tag sizes it to 12px and it takes the label's color.
